observations: In this run we observed the agent rebuild context at the start of each session by listing definitions and reading the file. At ck2 it read the whole file [2.3]. From ck3 on it used a def/class grep followed by many sed or offset reads ([3.2], [4.2]-[4.7], [7.2]-[7.15], [8.2]-[8.13]). New features were mostly written in /tmp and spliced in as new sections: the process/cache/archive block [4.9], the database [5.7], docker [6.19], and the migrations and upgrade blocks [7.16]-[7.17]. New code called existing helpers such as run_detailed, yaml_load, Option, confirm and docker_run (ck6-ck8 diffs). At ck4 the splice order caused a NameError at import, which the agent fixed by moving the block [4.11]-[4.12]. Verification was ad-hoc throughout: CLI runs, fake docker binaries and scratch scripts in /tmp ([6.21], [7.20]-[7.27], [8.24]-[8.33]). There were no test files and no notes. The agent re-ran old commands against a saved copy of the original at ck2 [2.22] and ck8 [8.35]. At ck8 that check put the fake docker on PATH [8.35], so it could not show that the new requirement check [8.20] makes earlier commands fail when docker is absent. That check accounts for 28 regressions. At ck6 the volume and network functions were written [6.19] but site create and site delete were never wired to call them.
